title: Unit Circle Definition
text: $$\cos\left(\frac{7\pi}{4}\right)$$ represents the x-coordinate of the point on the unit circle at the angle $$\frac{7\pi}{4}.$$\n##figure1.gif##

title: Reference Angle
text: The reference angle for $$\frac{7\pi}{4}$$ is $$\frac{\pi}{4}.$$ The absolute values of the coordinates are given by the legs of a $$45-45-90$$ triangle with hypotenuse $$1$$. The x-coordinate and y-coordinate lengths are equal and satisfy the Pythagorean theorem: $$1=\sqrt{x**2+x**2}=\sqrt{2}x,$$ so both coordinates are $$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.$$\n##figure2.gif##

title: Quadrant Sign
text: The angle $$\frac{7\pi}{4}$$ is in the fourth quadrant, where x-coordinates are positive. Therefore, $$\cos\left(\frac{7\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.$$\n##figure3.gif##
